sophia: Heads up — after landing the Novaline13B int4 build we see a reproducible quality regression on long-context summarization + rerank. ROUGE-L drops ~3.1 points vs fp16 and perplexity on the eval set jumps. Example diffs attached in the eval job output.

sophia: Repro steps: quantize with our usual gemm-int4 pipeline, run the longctx summarizer eval (seq=4096, beam=4), then rerank with embedding similarity. The strange part: short-context tasks are fine. Long-context only. :thinking:

sophia: Quick paste of the quant command we used:
```bash
python quantize.py --model-path models/novaline13b/ --dtype int4 --proj-order default --pos-mix rotary-scaled
```

daniel: can you paste the eval metric snippet? numbers + seed pls

sophia: sure — small snippet from CI run (seed 42):
```
# longctx-summarize eval
ROUGE-1: 42.8
ROUGE-2: 18.3
ROUGE-L: 38.2  # fp16 baseline was 41.3
Perplexity: 18.9  # fp16 baseline 14.2
Embedding rerank MRR: 0.72  # fp16 baseline 0.79
```

mira: interesting. sounds like a positional/kv handshake issue rather than proj quant noise. Did you check kv-cache warmup (first N tokens) error pattern?

sophia: yes, delta happens after ~256 tokens in most cases. If you truncate to 256 tokens eval matches fp16 closely. So long-range accumulation problem.

alex: could be the combination of our int4 proj-order packing + "pos_mix=rotary-scaled" being interpreted differently in the conversion script. I remember Novaline has a nonstandard projection ordering (headconcat across q/k). If proj-order is wrong, rotary phases will bind to wrong dims.

sophia: i tried switching proj-order to `head-major` and reran a small sample — perplexity dropped back ~0.6 but full eval still worse. Patch diff: changed converter flag `--proj-order head-major`

mira: can you dump a few tokens of kv keys (float32) pre/post conversion for same input start? if the rotary angle alignment is offset you'll see consistent phase drift across heads.

sophia: dumped key vectors for layer 10, head 3 — here's a tiny excerpt (fp16 vs int4->dequant):
```
fp16_k[0:8]: [ 0.0123, -0.0341, 0.0022, ... ]
int4_k[0:8]: [ 0.0118, -0.0339, 0.0019, ... ]  # small diff
phase_dot(fp,int4): 0.987
```
Not huge per-step, but error accumulates on long sequences.

alex: accumulation suggests a mismatch in rotary scaling factor or head-dim pairing. Two quick experiments: 1) disable rotary scaling (pos_mix -> rotary) and 2) apply per-head normalization after dequant to mimic fp16 norm.

sophia: kicked off both jobs. also flagged a conversion audit to ensure token id mapping wasn't shifted (vocab remap bug would create odd anchors).

ci-bot: job 8672 started: novaline-int4-disable-rotary-scaling-eval (triggered by sophia)

ops-bot: rolling log: allocated c6g.2xlarge for debug runs, ETA ~5m

daniel: another angle — our kv cache layout supports both contiguous and interleaved head storage. If converter wrote interleaved but runtime reads contiguous (or vice versa) you get headwise phase scramble that only shows up on long contexts. Did you check runtime layout flag?

sophia: runtime flag we use is `--kv-layout contiguous`. converter had default unset which apparently wrote interleaved. i'm re-running conversion with `--kv-layout contiguous` now.

mira: nice catch. that would be a perfect match for head-permutation style bugs — short contexts might hide it because cross-head interference is limited.

alex: if that fixes it we should add a conversion sanity check: for a small random seed input compute cross-head cosine similarity matrix between fp16 and quant dequant keys; assert diag>0.95. Add to converter smoke tests.

sophia: agreed — if the contiguous layout run passes i'll open a PR with smoke test. preliminary: the contiguous kv-layout rerun reduced ROUGE-L delta to 0.8 (still not perfect) and first-pass disabling rotary-scaling improved perplexity to 15.1. both together (contiguous + disable rotary-scale) essentially matches fp16 within noise.

daniel: so root causes: (A) converter wrote interleaved kv-layout by default, (B) proj-order assumption mismatch, (C) rotary-scale multiplier interacts badly with quant rounding. all three amplify on long context.

mira: next steps: 1) make converter write explicit layout metadata and fail if runtime mismatch, 2) add cross-head key diag check smoke, 3) add a quant-preserving rotary rescale heuristic (run-time adjust) for int4 builds, 4) run a full rerun of longctx benchmark.

sophia: i'll draft the converter patch and tests. leaving the CI jobs running — will paste final numbers. thanks all. :raised_hands:
